MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 7, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board of
Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:07 p.m.,
on June 7, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 2, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property: Turf Lane Open Space; 25361
  Turf Avenue (APN: 619-331-35) within the City of Mission Viejo; City Negotiator:
  City Manager Wilberg and City Attorney Curley; Negotiating Party:

______________________________________________________________________________
City Council Minutes  1  June 7, 2010
   Timberline Community Homeowners Association and Legal Counsel. Under
  Negotiation: Terms of Payment — Consideration and Quitclaim Deed from City to
  Timberline Community Homeowners Association.
CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation Pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission Viejo v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v. CUSD, Case
  No. 00207543.
CS3. Labor Negotiations — The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the
  City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

CS4. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour o 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Item CS1 the Council, by unanimous
vote, authorized the City quitclaiming its interest to the Turflane open space. The City will move that
transaction forward. On all other matters, the Council received information and gave direction but
there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Alexandra "Lexi" Marten of Trabuco Hills High School, Recipient of the
  Disneyland Resort Scholarship

  Mayor Kelley presented a Certificate of Commendation to Lexi Marten.

P2.  Commemorate the Dedication of the New Veterans Memorial at Saddleback College

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to the President of Saddleback College Tod
  Burnett, former President Dr. Richard McCullough, Board Vice President Nancy Padberg,
  and Chairman of the Veterans Memorial Task Force Marty Samuels.

P4.  Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements - Project Status
  The City Council received a project update from Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon.

______________________________________________________________________________
City Council Minutes  2  June 7, 2010
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Maurer, M.V.: discussed the Mission Viejo Library’s Family Place Program and its part in the
City Council’s strategic effort to "build community." For more information, residents can call
830-7100, extension 5107.

Judy Williams, M.V.: read a letter that she intends to send a neighbor whose home is not up to code
and she asked the Council to take action so she and her neighbors do not have to.

John Kiely, M.V.: former President of the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association, speaking on
behalf of resident Joyce Saltzgiver, urged residents to vote no on Measure D in tomorrow’s election.

Dan Avery, M.V.: stated that the opponents of Measure D have no imagination which leads them to
lie about non-existent threats in order to foster fear. He encouraged residents to vote tomorrow and
to vote no on Measure D.

Jim Yates, M.V.: discussing the Oso/Marguerite widening project, he noted that some of the
residents on Pinario and Monforte feel the project is incomplete. He asked the Council to encourage
city staff to move forward with the design for a sound wall and to negotiate with the residents who
have concerns.

Beth McConaughy, President of the Friends of the Library: discussed the installation of a sign
honoring deceased resident Lawrence D. Boyer who donated over $200,000 to the Friends of the
Mission Viejo Library. The Friends developed a committee and decided to place a sign over the local
history section to recognize Mr. Boyer’s very generous request.

Helen Workun, M.V.: stated that tomorrow is one of the most important days in the history of
Mission Viejo and she urged residents to vote no on Measure D.

Dennis O’Connor, M.V.: stated that Measure D is wrong on many levels and he asked what is wrong
with our proposition process that would allow this initiative to get on the ballot. He urged residents
to go out and vote no on Measure D tomorrow.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: asked residents to take a good close look at a recent No on Measure D flier
and she stated that it is unrealistic to think that businesses would want to come to Mission Viejo if
the measure passes.

Sherri Butterfield, M.V.: reminded residents that tomorrow is election day and among all the
candidates and propositions on the ballot, the one that has the most negative impact on Mission
Viejo is Measure D. She stated that the city’s planning process has served the residents very well and
she urged voters to protect Mission Viejo and join her in voting no on Measure D.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 7, 8, 10, 13, and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

12.  Oso Creek Kiosk and Way Finding Program

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release of the faithful

15.  2010 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $3,448,448.36 to All American

  2009-2010 Budget to Increase Funding for CIP 838; (3) adopt Resolution 10-24 Amending

  Alicia/Muirlands Intersection Improvements Project (CIP 887); and (4) adopt Resolution
  10-25 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-20 10 Budget to Increase Funding for CIP 838
  Resulting from the Ladera Reimbursements.

16.  FY 2010-11 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  (1) Approved the FY 2010-11 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of
  Orange for an amount not to exceed $15,183,451; and (2) authorized the City Manager to
  approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed
  $65,000 for FY 2010-11.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 13. Issuance of Permit Pursuant to Municipal Code Section 11:13:015(b) for Palmia

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Lt. Mike Gavin commented on the extent of the permit and his evaluation of the proposal to
  exterminate rabbits.

  Kelly Barraza and Reid Barraza, M.V.: expressed opposition to the proposal to exterminate
  rabbits and presented suggestions for natural rabbit deterrents.

OLD BUSINESS

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented the
  staff report.

  Jennifer Farr, Mayer Hoffman McCann P.C.: stated that her firm has begun the preliminary
  audit procedures for the year ended June 30, 2010, and she asked the Council Members if they

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  receive correspondence from Mayer Hoffman McCann P.C., the City’s independent auditors,
  regarding the upcoming financial statement audit for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2010, and

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury

20.  Integrated Solid Waste Management Services Agreement

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report and noted that the written report includes a
  copy of the consultant’s detailed evaluation, including their recommendation and staff’s
  recommendation for continuation of the process.

  The following provided final comments and discussed their company’s resources and
  qualifications: Dean Ruffridge, CR&R: Charissa MacAfee, Waste Management; Brett Barbre
  and Gary Clifford, Athens Services and Jason Rush, Ware Disposal.

  Joe Sloan, Sloan Vazquez, answered questions of the City Council.

  The following presented a written comment in favor of awarding a contract to CR&R: Max and

PRESENTATIONS (Continued)

P3.  Proclaim June 14, 2010, to be United States Army Day and Commend Lt. Colonel
  Miguel Howe for his Service in Mission Viejo as Commanding Officer of the Southern
  California Army Recruiting Battalion (Battle Sharks)

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation and commendation to Lt. Colonel Miguel Howe
  for his service as Commanding Officer of the Southern California Army Recruiting Battalion
  (Battle Sharks). Lt. Col. Howe introduced Lt. Col. Tom Hansbarger who will assume
  command of the battalion when Col. Howe deploys to Iraq.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:20 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:37 p.m.
with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ledesma returned at 8:41 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to discuss a
  potential contract with Athens and Waste Management and discontinue discussing CR&R as
  an option.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct staff and
  Sloan Vazquez Consulting, LLC, to negotiate a proposed final Agreement with Waste
  Management for the provision of Integrated Solid Waste Management Services and to present
  said Agreement for City Council’s consideration at a future meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

______________________________________________________________________________
City Council Minutes  7  June 7, 2010

 8.  Records for Electronic Retention - Community Development and Public Works

City Manager’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

25.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
______________________________________________________________________________
City Council Minutes  10  June 7, 2010
   Council Member Schlicht noted that while she was honored to attend the Marty Russo Park
  dedication, she personally disagrees with the policy to pay mileage to Council Members who
  attend events for the city.

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in
  the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma announced that he was saddened to hear that the son of South Orange
County Community College District Trustee, Don Wagner, passed away and he asked Mayor
Kelley to adjourn the meeting in memory of Paul Wagner.

Council Member Schlicht

26.  Transparency in Government

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she originally placed this item on the agenda after she
  was denied access to the waste management proposals but she since received the copies so it
  is a moot point.

Council Member Schlicht announced that she believes there was an unintentional Brown Act
violation as a result of Mayor Pro Tem Leckness’ discussions about the trash contract with more
than one Council Member. She reiterated that it was accidental but she wanted to bring it to
everyone’s attention. She also stated that Council Member Ury launches insults at her but when she
questions and challenges his integrity, it is called a slur. She stated that the discussions tonight
proved that we need to give more power to the public and she feels Measure D will protect the
residents from any zone changes. Council Member Schlicht ended her comments by quoting from
Thomas Paine and she reminded residents to exercise their civic duty and vote tomorrow.

Council Member Ury Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness reminded residents of the election tomorrow and announced that he will
be voting no on Measure D. He encouraged residents to read the materials and make their own
decisions. Mr. Leckness also announced that he visited the Murray Community Center earlier today
and he had the honor of attending a very unique class called Laughter Yoga.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley stated that she is very active on behalf of the city and she attends many events,
sometimes two or three a day. She does give freely of her time and it takes away from her personal
business. She noted that she spends more than 40 hours a week for her position on the City Council
and while she has been criticized for accepting reimbursement for mileage, she asked the Council for
direction if they want her to stop these activities. She acknowledged that Council Member Schlicht
attended an event last month and chose not to seek reimbursement and that is certainly her
______________________________________________________________________________
City Council Minutes  11  June 7, 2010
 prerogative. Mayor Kelley announced that she attended the KSBR Birthday Bash along with Mayor
Pro Tem Leckness and she thanked the city staff for assisting with the event. The city’s Memorial
Day Ceremony was held the following day and again, the city staff did a wonderful job and she is
very proud that we are able to honor those who have given their lives for our country. On June 1,
2010, the city held an Emergency Preparedness Academy graduation and she attended to observe the
ceremony and the disaster scene reenactment. She is very pleased that the city hosts these academies
and she is proud of the residents who participate. She thanked staff, the Sheriff’s Department and the
Orange County Fire Authority personnel who help make the program such a success. Mayor Kelley
announced that the Marine Adoption Committee is hosting a baby shower for the families of our
adopted Marines and they are seeking donations of various baby items for gift baskets. She also
announced that she attended a Mission Hospital Trauma Center 30th Anniversary celebration.
Mission Hospital is the top diagnostic hospital in the world and Mayor Kelley observed that we are
very fortunate to have such a facility in our community. She also recounted her attendance at the
Relay for Life where she participated as a Team Captain. It was a very successful event, raising over
$160,000 and she encouraged residents to send donations if they haven’t already done so. Mayor
Kelley announced that the Community of Character word of the month of June is citizenship and she
reminded residents to vote in tomorrow’s election.

ADJOURNED

At the hour of 10:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Maria Williams and Paul Wagner to Monday,
June 21, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 21, 2010

City Council Minutes  12  June 7, 2010
